title: Photo-isolation chemistry for high-resolution and deep spatial transcriptome with mouse tissue sections
author: Honda, Kimura, et al.
materials: The efficiency of in situ reverse transcription (RT) is best with fresh-frozen sections, followed by formalin-fixed frozen and paraffin sections (Figure 1A). However, formalin-fixed tissues have greater advantages in preserving tissue morphologies and preventing the dissipative loss of marker molecules for the visualization of ROIs, such as immunostaining and reporter protein antigens. In our experience, proteins that are less interactive with other molecules, such as GFP, are lost easily and need to be fixed (Figure 1B), whereas transcription factors and the proteins composing liquid-liquid phase separation are often detected without fixation. Furthermore, because RNAs are bound by various proteins and covalently cross-linked by formalin fixation, a permeabilization step is necessary to eliminate these interferences before in situ RT. In our experience, briefly soaking the sections in HCl solution or heating them in TE solution is effective for fresh-frozen sections, whereas only the latter is effective for formalin-fixed tissues. Therefore, with a tissue for the first trial, both unfixed and fixed frozen sections were prepared and permeabilized with HCl or TE before immunostaining for ROI labeling (Figure 1A). If ROIs can be identified simply by nuclear staining, the fresh-frozen section is the best choice. If only paraffin sections were available, permeabilization with TE alone was tested. Therefore, the optimal conditions should be selected by evaluating the balance of tissue morphology, preservation of marker antigens, and efficiency of in situ RT.Figure 1Selection guide for fixation and permeabilization(A) The selection chart for tissue fixation and permeabilization. The fresh-frozen section provides the greatest efficiency for in situ RT when permeabilized with HCl or TE, but is inferior to the fixed samples in terms of preservation of tissue morphology and antigen cross-linkage. Formalin-fixed frozen or paraffin sections preserve tissue morphology and antigen cross-linkage for immunolabeling to a greater extent.(B) Brain sections from the hippocampal region in GFP-expressing mice are shown to explain the importance of antigen cross-linkage. GFP was mostly lost in fresh-frozen sections after HCl or TE permeabilization, but preserved in tissues with longer formalin fixation, even after heating with TE. Scale bars, 200 μm.

steps.title: Prepare and permeabilize tissue sections
steps.instruction: Section fresh‑frozen tissue and either briefly soak in HCl solution or heat in Tris‑EDTA (TE) solution; for formalin‑fixed frozen or paraffin sections, heat only in TE solution. Choose the condition that best balances tissue morphology, antigen preservation, and in situ reverse‑transcription efficiency.

substeps.instruction: Fresh‑frozen: brief HCl soak or TE heating.
Formalin‑fixed frozen or paraffin: TE heating only.

steps.title: Optional immunostaining of ROIs
steps.instruction: Label regions of interest with primary and secondary antibodies while avoiding reagents that require UV excitation (<425 nm).

substeps.instruction: Aspirate PBS, add 50 µL blocking solution, incubate at room temperature (RT) 15 min in a humidified chamber.
Aspirate blocking solution, add 50 µL primary antibody diluted in blocking solution, incubate at RT 2 h in a humidified chamber.
Aspirate primary antibody, wash sections three times with 50 µL TBST.
Add 50 µL secondary antibody diluted in blocking solution, incubate at RT 1 h in a humidified chamber.
Aspirate secondary antibody, wash sections three times with 50 µL TBST.

steps.title: Optional nuclear staining
steps.instruction: Stain nuclei with Nuclear Violet LCS1 (1:500) without uncaging NPOM groups.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate TBST, add 50 µL Nuclear Violet LCS1 (1:500 in blocking solution), incubate at RT 15 min in a humidified chamber (can be done together with secondary antibody incubation).
Aspirate staining solution, wash sections three times with 50 µL TBST.

steps.title: Photo‑irradiate to uncage primers
steps.instruction: Expose the labeled ROIs to the appropriate wavelength light (avoid <425 nm) to uncage the NPOM‑protected RT primers, thereby activating cDNA synthesis in the selected region.

steps.title: Purify cDNA:mRNA hybrids
steps.instruction: Use a Qiagen MinElute spin column to clean up the cDNA:mRNA hybrid mixture.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 volumes of Buffer PB (≈400 µL) to 1 volume of sample (≈80 µL).
Vortex and spin down at 1,400 × g, RT, 2 s.
Apply the lysate to a MinElute Spin Column (max 750 µL).
Centrifuge at 15,300 × g, RT, 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Add 750 µL Buffer PE to the column.
Centrifuge at 15,300 × g, RT, 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Centrifuge at 15,300 × g, RT, 2 min; discard flow‑through.
Transfer the column to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Add 17 µL nuclease‑free water, incubate RT 1 min.
Centrifuge at 15,300 × g, RT, 2 min; discard flow‑through.
Pause point: store at –20 °C (light‑shielded) for ≥1 month if needed.

steps.title: Purify aRNA after IVT
steps.instruction: Clean up the in‑vitro‑transcribed aRNA using enzymatic treatments and RNAClean XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL TURBO DNase (MEGAscript T7 kit).
Spin 1,400 × g, RT, 2 s; incubate 37 °C 15 min, then place on ice.
Add 3 µL ExoSAP‑IT Express PCR Product Cleanup.
Spin 1,400 × g, RT, 2 s; incubate 37 °C 5 min, then place on ice.
Add 5.5 µL Fragmentation Buffer, vortex.
Spin 1,400 × g, RT, 2 s; incubate 94 °C 3 min, then place on ice.
Add 2.75 µL 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0), vortex.
Spin 1,400 × g, RT, 2 s; place on magnetic stand, incubate RT 5 min.
Collect 28 µL supernatant into a new 0.2 mL 8‑strip PCR tube.
Add 50.4 µL RNAClean XP beads (1.8 × sample volume), vortex.
Spin 1,400 × g, RT, 2 s; incubate RT 10 min.
Place on magnetic stand, wait ≥5 min.
Remove supernatant carefully.
Add 200 µL 70 % ethanol, incubate RT 30 s; remove supernatant.
Add another 200 µL 70 % ethanol, incubate RT 30 s; remove supernatant.
Spin 1,400 × g, RT, 2 s.
Place on magnetic stand, incubate RT 1 min.
Remove supernatant, air‑dry beads 2 min (ensure no ethanol remains).
Resuspend beads in 6.5 µL nuclease‑free water, incubate RT ≥2 min.
Spin 1,400 × g, RT, 2 s; place on magnetic stand, incubate RT 5 min.
Collect 4.5 µL supernatant into a new 0.2 mL 8‑strip PCR tube.
Pause point: store at –80 °C for ≥1 month if needed.

steps.title: Prepare libraries and sequence
steps.instruction: Construct sequencing libraries and run paired‑end Illumina sequencing, adding PhiX spike‑in and targeting appropriate read depth.

substeps.instruction: Perform paired‑end sequencing on an Illumina platform (e.g., HiSeq or NovaSeq) following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Add PhiX control at 5 % of the final library.
Aim for 10–20 million reads per sample (Read 1: 12 cycles for UMI and barcode + 18 cycles; Read 2: ≥50 cycles for cDNA).

steps.title: Process sequencing data
steps.instruction: Extract barcodes/UMIs, trim adapters, align reads, count features, and identify differentially expressed genes.

substeps.instruction: Extract barcodes and UMIs: `umi_tools extract -I read1.fastq --read2-in=read2.fastq --bc-pattern=NNNNNNCCCCCC --read2-stdout`.
Trim adapters: `trim_galore -a GATCGTCGGACT`.
Align reads with HISAT2 to the appropriate reference genome (e.g., GRCm38).

Count reads per gene: `featureCounts -a GRCm38.gtf -R BAM input.bam` followed by `samtools index input.featureCounts.bam` and `umi_tools count --method=unique --per-gene --per-cell --gene-tag=XT -I input.featureCounts.bam`.
Identify differentially expressed genes using the DESeq2 R package and perform downstream analyses such as PCA with `prcomp`.

description: Photo-isolation chemistry (PIC) is a spatial transcriptome method for locally defined areas with the advantages of high spatial resolution and detection depth, ranging from large to small areas such as brain fields, embryonic tissues, single cells, and intracellular structures. PIC comprises the following five processes: (1) Sections are prepared from fresh or fixed tissues and permeabilized with HCl or Tris-EDTA (TE); (2) mRNAs are reverse-transcribed in situ with photo-caged primers; (3) the regions of interest (ROIs) are labeled by immunostaining and/or nuclear staining; (4) cDNA-conjugated primers are uncaged by photo-irradiation; (5) uncaged cDNAs are selectively amplified by in vitro transcription (IVT) before sequencing. Once tissue sections are prepared, two days are required to prepare sequencing libraries with standard molecular biology equipment and expertise.
